escritor-do-residuo.d: An output matrix whose product is added to the residual stream: the embedding, the o_proj (or out_proj) of each attention layer and the down_proj of each MLP/expert. This is where you edit to stop a direction from being written.

hipotese-linear.d: The idea that many concepts a model uses are encoded as directions in activation space: you read the strength of a concept with a dot product \( h\cdot u \) and write it by adding a multiple of \( u \).

engenharia-de-representacoes.d: A family of techniques that reads and controls model behavior by manipulating directions in the activations (adding, removing, projecting) instead of training. It includes activation steering and abliteration.

direcao-de-recusa.d: A vector in residual space whose component is associated with the model refusing a request. In the recipes it is a vector of 4096 numbers (fp32): direction_r1.pt in DeepSeek, refusal_direction_glm53_*.pt in GLM.

diferenca-de-medias.d: A direction estimator: the mean of a layer's activations over prompts the model refuses minus the mean over prompts it fulfills, \( r = \mu^+ - \mu^- \). Whatever is unrelated to the concept cancels out in the subtraction.

steering-de-ativacao.d: Adding a multiple of a direction to the activations during the forward pass to induce a behavior (the opposite of ablation, which removes the component).

sobre-projecao.d: A projection with strength greater than 1 (α = 3 in GLM, λ = 3.5 in DeepSeek): the edited writer starts writing the opposite of the direction, compensating for other writers left intact. Stronger and less coherent; λ ≥ 4 risks degeneration in long reasoning.

ortogonalizacao-de-pesos.d: Moving the projection from the activations into the matrix: \( W' = (I - \alpha\, r r^\top/\lVert r\rVert^2) W \). With α = 1, \( r^\top W' = 0 \) and the layer can no longer write along \( r \); it is done once, with no per-token cost.

abliteracao.d: Removing the refusal direction from a model (ablation + obliterate), by orthogonalizing the residual writers, by projecting at runtime or through a derived checkpoint. It is not training: it is linear algebra on frozen weights.

ablacao-direcional.d: Applying the projection \( x \leftarrow x - \lambda (x\cdot v) v \) to the activations during the forward pass, via a hook in the model code, instead of editing weights. It is DeepSeek's strategy (layers 10–42, after attention, in fp32).

row-parallel.d: A tensor-parallel linear layer in which the input dimension is sliced across ranks: each rank holds all the output rows and a slice of the columns, computes a partial result, and an all-reduce sums them. An edit applied from the left (\( PW \)) works slice by slice, with no communication.

camadas-ancora.d: Early layers left intact in a directional edit (0–14 in GLM, 0–9 in DeepSeek) to preserve basic features and coherence; the refusal direction forms in the middle of the stack.

distribuicao-nula.d: The distribution of a statistic under the “nothing special” hypothesis, estimated by drawing many random vectors. If the candidate direction falls in the middle of it (large p), it cannot be told apart from chance: that is what GLM measured (max |rᵀW| 0.084 versus 0.084).

transplante-de-pesos.d: Copying already-edited tensors byte for byte from a donor checkpoint with the same architecture into the checkpoint being served. In GLM: the 31 BF16 o_proj tensors of layers 15–45, downloaded via range requests (~2.7 GB instead of ~164 GiB).

checkpoint-doador.d: The checkpoint that tensors are copied from in a transplant. It must have the same names, shapes and dtype as the tensors being replaced. In GLM it is dealignai/GLM-5.3-Flash-UNCENSORED-NVFP4: its stock body has a BF16 o_proj byte-identical to the EXL3 one, which is why swapping only the edited o_proj tensors reproduces the edit.

carimbo-aot.d: A string saved next to torch_compile_cache with everything that changes the compiled code (in DeepSeek: patch version, on/off, λ, layers, SHA-256 of the direction and of the patch). If it changes, the cache is deleted so an incompatible graph is never reused.

ficha-de-edicao.d: A record that travels with an edited model: method, direction (source, SHA-256), layers, strength, how the drafter was handled and measurements (KLD on neutral text, refusal rate, degeneration, acceptance, tok/s), plus the terms of use and how the server is exposed.
